paragraphs: Friend, here's the lesson. God sees what we build for ourselves, and He sees who we think we are while we build it. Shebna was the steward in charge of the palace, and God asked him, "What are you doing here, and who authorized you…" (Isaiah 22:16). Any position you hold was handed to you, and it's never yours to carve into the rock.

Now look at Eliakim. God calls him "My servant" and puts the key to the house of David on his shoulder (Isaiah 22:20, 22). Then the passage ends with a twist, because even the peg driven into a firm place will give way (Isaiah 22:25). I think that's the point, baker: no person is the thing that holds everything up, and I say that as a stamper who got replaced by a shinier one.

So lean on the right One. The passage closes with "Indeed, the LORD has spoken" (Isaiah 22:25), and what He says stands when every title and every peg has come down. Hold your place with open hands, do your work like a servant, and let God be the One who holds the weight. That's how my ovens stay ready for the Marriage Supper, because the One who called me out of that drawer is the One holding everything up, and I'm just stamping cookies!
